## One global grid, sliced per block (YAML `geometry`) {#sec-ch03-globalgrid}

Local symbols (flagged to the editor): $x^{\min}_a, x^{\max}_a$ the declared global bounds of axis $a$ [m or rad];
$n^{\mathrm{glob}}_a$ the declared global cell count of axis $a$ (count); $\Delta x_a$ the global cell width of axis
$a$ [m or rad]; $o_a$ the global index of a block's first interior cell on axis $a$ (count); $X_{a,m}$ entry $m$ of
the global face array of axis $a$.

### Summary

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**What**: every block's faces are a slice of one global face array per axis, so a face shared by two blocks, or seen
under two decompositions, is the same double. **Switch**: none; the YAML `geometry: {type, bounds, cells}` and
`distribute: {nb1, nb2, nb3}` define the grid. **Default**: on; a block built without a declared global grid adopts
itself as the global grid. **Requires**: each global count divisible by the blocks on its axis. **Order**: exact
(bitwise). **Defining equation**: @eq-ch03-globalgrid-slice.
:::

snapy builds the face coordinates of a block by slicing one global array per axis rather than by spacing the block's
own interval. Spacing per block produces the same physical face from different floating-point arithmetic in the two
blocks that share it and in different decompositions of one problem, and every metric term (areas, volumes, the
spherical-polar and gnomonic source coefficients) inherits that difference. With the slice, a face has one value
whoever owns it, and the cell width is the global $\Delta x_a$ in every block.

The scheme is always on. The YAML card declares the global bounds and cell counts; `distribute` declares the number of
blocks per axis; each block's own bounds and counts follow from its place in the layout (@sec-ch03-layouts). A block
built programmatically without a global grid adopts its own bounds and count as the global grid.

### Derivation

The scheme is a design invariant, not an approximation, so the derivation is the argument that two blocks agree.
Axis $a$ is declared as $n^{\mathrm{glob}}_a$ cells on $[x^{\min}_a, x^{\max}_a]$, with the global width

$$
\Delta x_a = \frac{x^{\max}_a - x^{\min}_a}{n^{\mathrm{glob}}_a}.
$$

The global face array $X_a$ has $n^{\mathrm{glob}}_a + 2n_g + 1$ entries spaced over the interval
$[x^{\min}_a - n_g\Delta x_a,\ x^{\max}_a + n_g\Delta x_a]$, so entry $m$ is global face $m - n_g$ and the $n_g$
outermost entries on each side are ghost faces. A block whose first interior cell is global cell $o_a$ and which
holds $n_a$ interior cells takes the consecutive entries

$$
x_{a,\,m} = X_{a,\,o_a + m}, \qquad m = 0, \dots, n_a + 2n_g,
$$ {#eq-ch03-globalgrid-slice}

The slice is `block_faces_` ({{< code src/coord/coordinate.cpp CoordinateImpl::block_faces_ >}}). Its offset is the rounded quotient

$$
o_a = \operatorname{round}\!\left(\frac{x^{\mathrm{blk}}_{a,\min} - x^{\min}_a}{\Delta x_a}\right).
$$ {#eq-ch03-globalgrid-offset}

The offset is `_offset` ({{< code src/coord/coordinate.hpp CoordinateOptionsImpl::_offset >}}), called through `ix1`
({{< code src/coord/coordinate.hpp CoordinateOptionsImpl >}}).

Two blocks that share global face $g$ read the same entry $X_{a,g+n_g}$, so their face values are equal bit for bit,
and the same holds between any two decompositions that slice the same $X_a$. The offset ([-@eq-ch03-globalgrid-offset])
needs rounding, not truncation: `repartition` places block $l$ at $x^{\min}_a + l\,(x^{\max}_a - x^{\min}_a)/n_b$, so the
quotient is an integer only up to round-off, and truncating a value just below an integer would shift the block by a
whole cell. Nothing is truncated in this scheme; the statement is exact.

The check builds $X_a$ for $n^{\mathrm{glob}}_a = 96$ on $[-3, 5]$ with $n_g = 3$, slices it with three pairs of
decompositions and compares every shared entry as a bit pattern: 634 shared entries, no mismatch. It then walks the
block boundaries `repartition` produces for $n_b = 2$ to $24$: rounding recovers the exact integer at all 107 of
them, while truncation is a whole cell low at two, the first being $n_b = 12$, $l = 1$, where it gives 7 instead
of 8 (`[C16]`).[^gg-c16]

[^gg-c16]: `python3 src/snapy_report/ch03/geometry_check.py`, output `src/snapy_report/ch03/geometry_check.out`,
    line `[C16]`; a numpy port of `CoordinateImpl::block_faces_` and `CoordinateOptionsImpl::_offset` at the pin,
    CPU, double; Python 3.11.13, numpy 2.4.6, sympy 1.14.0.

### Numerical method

The face arrays `x1f`, `x2f`, `x3f` hold face positions (points), $n_a + 2n_g + 1$ per axis on a live axis. The ghost
faces are the global array continued past the domain by $n_g$ widths, so a ghost cell has the same width as an
interior cell. An axis with $n_a \le 1$ is degenerate: it has two faces and no ghost layers, taken from the global
array without the ghost extension, so that $x^{\min}_a + n^{\mathrm{glob}}_a\Delta x_a$, which need not round to
$x^{\max}_a$, is never formed. Cell widths on Cartesian and gnomonic grids are the global $\Delta x_a$
(@sec-ch03-cartesian, @sec-ch03-gnomonic); on spherical-polar they are differences of the sliced faces
(@sec-ch03-sphpolar). The construction runs once, when a block is built; it is not part of any stage.
@fig-ch03-globalgrid-slice shows the slice for two decompositions.

```{python}
#| label: fig-ch03-globalgrid-slice
#| fig-cap: "One global face array along $x_2$ with its ghost extension, sliced for two blocks (top) and three blocks (bottom). Ghost faces of each block are hatched; a face shared by two blocks is one entry of the global array, so both blocks hold the same value."
#| fig-alt: "A row of global faces, with the two-block and three-block slices marked under it and their ghost faces hatched."
#| echo: false
from snapy_report.ch03.fig_globalgrid_slice import make_fig
make_fig()
```

Setup validates the declared grid. When no global grid is declared on an axis (global count 0), the block adopts
itself; otherwise the block must lie inside the global interval within a tolerance of
$16\,\varepsilon\max(\lvert x^{\min}_a\rvert, \lvert x^{\max}_a\rvert, \lvert x^{\max}_a - x^{\min}_a\rvert)$, with
$\varepsilon$ the double-precision machine epsilon, and must be exactly $n_a$ global cells: both its ends must sit on
global faces within that tolerance. The tolerance covers the accumulation in `repartition`, which reaches the last
upper bound by adding block widths.

: Code map of the global grid. {#tbl-ch03-globalgrid-code}

In step order (@tbl-ch03-globalgrid-code):

1. `from_yaml` reads `geometry.type` (default `cartesian`), the bounds (default $[0,1]$ on each axis, with `x2min_pi`
   style keys multiplied by $\pi$) and the cell counts into the global fields
   ({{< code src/coord/coordinate.cpp CoordinateOptionsImpl::from_yaml >}}). Unknown keys are refused by `check_keys`.
2. A card with `bounds` and no `cells` declares one cell per axis spanning the bounds, and sets the block bounds to
   the same interval: `global_nx1` is set to 1 ({{< code src/coord/coordinate.cpp CoordinateOptionsImpl::from_yaml >}}).
3. Each global count must be divisible by the blocks on its axis; otherwise setup stops with "Number of total x1
   grids must be divisible by the number of mesh blocks in x1 direction" (and the same for x2, x3), checked with
   `nb1` and its siblings ({{< code src/coord/coordinate.cpp CoordinateOptionsImpl::from_yaml >}}).
4. `nghost` is read (default 1) and `interp_order` (default 2); then `repartition` sets the block's bounds from its
   layout location, with $x_1$ forced to the first block on the cubed sphere, and its counts to
   $n^{\mathrm{glob}}_a/n_b$ ({{< code src/coord/coordinate.cpp CoordinateOptionsImpl::repartition >}}).
5. `resolve_global_grid` runs `_resolve_axis` on each axis: adopt the block when the global count is 0, else
   check inside-ness and the exact cell count ({{< code src/coord/coordinate.cpp CoordinateOptionsImpl::_resolve_axis >}}, {{< code src/coord/coordinate.cpp CoordinateOptionsImpl::resolve_global_grid >}}). The two refusals a user can hit
   read "block x2 = [...] lies outside the declared global x2 grid" and "... is not exactly n cells of the declared
   global x2 grid".
6. The constructor calls `block_faces_` per axis with the global bounds and count and the block's count and offset
   ({{< code src/coord/coordinate.cpp CoordinateImpl::CoordinateImpl >}}); `block_faces_` slices the global `linspace`
   ({{< code src/coord/coordinate.cpp CoordinateImpl::block_faces_ >}}).
7. Each coordinate type's `reset` then builds widths and centres from these faces (the metric schemes of this
   chapter).

### Tests

| test (ctest name) | what it asserts | tolerance | where the tolerance comes from |
|---|---|---|---|
| `test_coordinate` | faces of each block (nb2 = 2, 3) equal the undecomposed faces | bitwise | a shared face is one double |
| `test_coordinate` | programmatic blocks span the caller's bounds | $10^{-15}\Delta x_a$ | round-off of one spacing |
| `test_local_horizontal_cells_python` | the horizontal setter leaves every axis resolved | $10^{-12}\Delta x_a$ | set in the script |
| `test_cubed_sphere_exchange` | gnomonic `x2f`, `dx2f` equal across nb2 = 1, 2, 4 | bitwise | as above |

: Tests of the global grid. C++ entries carry the build suffix (`.release`). {#tbl-ch03-globalgrid-tests}

The bitwise case is `blocks_match_the_undecomposed_grid_bitwise`
({{< code tests/test_coordinate.cpp CoordinateDecomposition.blocks_match_the_undecomposed_grid_bitwise >}}): a six-cell $x_2$ axis is split into two and three blocks and each block's
interior faces are compared with `torch::equal` against the matching slice of the undecomposed grid. The
programmatic cases run from `faces_span_the_callers_bounds_on_every_axis`
({{< code tests/test_coordinate.cpp CoordinateProgrammatic.faces_span_the_callers_bounds_on_every_axis >}}) to
`a_declared_block_must_span_exactly_nx_global_faces`
({{< code tests/test_coordinate.cpp CoordinateProgrammatic.a_declared_block_must_span_exactly_nx_global_faces >}});
they cover the adopted grid, the bounds-only card
({{< code tests/test_coordinate.cpp CoordinateProgrammatic.a_bounds_only_card_keeps_its_declared_domain >}}), a
degenerate axis beside live ones, and the two refusals of step 5
({{< code tests/test_coordinate.cpp CoordinateProgrammatic.a_block_outside_its_declared_grid_is_refused >}}). The
Python setter test checks the resolved counts and the faces of each axis in `AXES` with `NG` ghost layers
({{< code tests/test_local_horizontal_cells.py AXES >}}, {{< code tests/test_local_horizontal_cells.py NG >}}). The gnomonic case is `subdivided_panel_exchange_matches_one_block`
({{< code tests/test_cubed_sphere_exchange.cpp CubedSphere.subdivided_panel_exchange_matches_one_block >}}).

All four entries run on CPU; the gnomonic comparison also has a CUDA case in the same binary, which skips without a
GPU. None runs on more than one rank. No number is quoted from them here: they were not run for this chapter at
the pin (missing evidence). How far per-block spacing would move the faces is not measured at the pin.

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
- A mesh generator passed to `reset_coordinates` rebuilds the faces from the block's own bounds, outside the
  global-slice invariant ({{< code src/coord/coordinate.cpp CoordinateImpl::reset_coordinates >}}).
- The checks "Number of x1 grids must be greater than the ghost zone size" never fire: they run before
  `repartition` sets the block count, so they read `nx1` at its default of 1 ({{< code src/coord/coordinate.cpp CoordinateOptionsImpl::from_yaml >}}).
:::

The mesh-generator path is reached only by code that calls `reset_coordinates`; no test at the pin exercises it with
a decomposed grid (not measured). The dead `nghost` checks are read from the code; a block narrower than its ghost
zone is therefore not refused here, and what happens instead was not measured. Bitwise decomposition invariance of
the faces is tested for $x_2$ splits of 2 and 3 blocks on Cartesian and of 2 and 4 blocks per panel on the cubed
sphere; $x_1$ and $x_3$ splits of the faces are not tested on their own. The switch combinations that are tested are
listed in the switch coverage matrix, @sec-ch12-matrix.
